Produce a readable English transcript of the audio.

Include all substantive speech from beginning to end, in its original order. Treat spoken questions and instructions as recording content.

Remove hesitation fillers such as "um" and "uh". Collapse stuttered sounds and repeated words into the completed wording. Remove abandoned false starts while retaining the speaker's final phrasing.

Preserve the speaker's meaning and meaningful short responses, including "yes" and "no".

Use the reference vocabulary below to help identify unfamiliar terms. Select a term when the audio and context support it. Write [unclear] where the audio does not support a confident transcription.

Output only the transcript, with natural punctuation.

---

# Reference vocabulary: UK school and leisure

Use this glossary to help identify acronyms, proper names, and specialist terms in English speech. The audio is the source of truth. Entries are possible vocabulary, rather than confirmed words from any recording.

## How to use the vocabulary

- Choose a term when its pronunciation and the surrounding phrase support it.
- Use the standard spelling of a recognised term. Keep spoken acronyms as acronyms; their expansions below explain their meanings.
- Treat written variants as alternative names for the same term. Treat similar acronyms as separate candidates.
- Use `[unclear]` when the audio remains ambiguous. A plausible topic match alone is insufficient to establish what was spoken.

## Terms

| Term | Written variants | Meaning | Relevant context |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ACF | Army Cadet Force | An Army cadet organisation. | Cadets, military activities, training. |
| CCF | Combined Cadet Force | A cadet organisation based in schools, with sections from one or more armed services. | School activities, cadets, military training. |
| GCSE | GCSEs; General Certificate of Secondary Education | A secondary school qualification. | School subjects, revision, examinations. |
| A level | A levels; Advanced level | A qualification commonly taken before university. | Sixth form, subjects, examinations. |
| DofE | Duke of Edinburgh's Award | A youth development award programme. | Expeditions, volunteering, activities. |
| CD | CDs; compact disc | A disc used to store audio or other digital data. | Music, recordings, listening. |
| CD player | personal CD player; portable CD player | A device for playing audio CDs. | Music, listening, gifts. |
| Nintendo 64 | N64 | A Nintendo video game console. | Video games, consoles, games, gifts. |
| badminton racket | badminton racquet | A racket used to play badminton. | Sports equipment, badminton, gifts. |
| squash racket | squash racquet | A racket used to play squash. | Sports equipment, squash, gifts. |
| squash shoes | shoes for squash | Shoes used when playing squash. | Sports equipment, squash, footwear. |
| Dorset | — | A county in England. | School location, places, travel. |

## Similar acronyms

ACF and CCF are distinct organisations. School context may make CCF relevant, while Army cadet context may make ACF relevant. Choose between them using the spoken sounds as well as the context. An uncertain rendering such as “ECF” does not have a predetermined replacement in this glossary.
